model.name: Plan / Schedule
model.purpose: Intentions bound to time: a coherent set of intended actions, the commitments that make some of those intentions binding, and the schedule bindings that fix them to instants, intervals, recurrences and orderings so an agent can compare intention with later performance.
model.scope_statement: This aggregate covers plans as sets of intended steps, schedule entries that bind those steps to time, recurrence and exception generation, precedence and hierarchy among planned items, organizer and attendee participation as a scheduling commitment surface, named baselines and revision identity, and the disclosure, classification and retention rules that govern sharing a plan or a free-busy projection. It is format-neutral: iCalendar, JSCalendar, PROV, P-Plan and FHIR CarePlan are alignments and interchange projections, not the model itself. A date is never an identifier. Occurrence qualification uses a master identifier plus a recurrence qualifier, not a calendar date used as a surrogate key.
in_scope: Identity, classification, purpose, horizon and lifecycle of a plan as a set of intentions
Planned steps or actions with intended verb, target, priority, expected effort and planned inputs and outputs
Assumptions and constraints the plan relies on
Binding commitments and RSVP-style participation obligations about planned items
Time bindings: start, end or due, duration, floating versus zoned time, all-day or show-without-time flags, transparency
Recurrence rules, additional and excluded occurrence dates, occurrence overrides and this-and-future splits
Calendar scale and non-Gregorian recurrence where a primary recurrence profile supplies it
Time zone identification, daylight-discontinuity handling and temporal reference system
Free-busy and availability intervals as a reduced projection of a schedule
Precedence constraints including finish-to-start and the other three precedence-diagramming types, with lead and lag
Hierarchical parent, child and sibling composition and grouping keys
Organizer, attendee, delegation and acting-on-behalf roles in scheduling exchanges
Scheduling methods: publish, request, reply, add, cancel, refresh, counter and decline-counter
Revision identity combining master identifier, occurrence qualifier, sequence number and stamp time
Named schedule baselines used as comparison snapshots
Provenance of a plan as an entity, including association with a planning agent and correspondence of execution to planned steps
Classification, sharing projections, ownership, access exceptions and retention or cancellation semantics
out_of_scope: Recorded completed acts and their actual start, end and outcomes, which belong to the act or action sibling
Standing process, procedure or workflow definitions independent of a particular intended instance
Project, programme or portfolio containers that bind a schedule but are not themselves a plan
Task as a work-item sibling that may reference a plan or schedule
Person, organization, group or software-agent master identity
Location, site and geospatial master data beyond an occurrence location reference
Resource, asset, capacity, inventory and skill catalogues, including resource leveling
Legal contract, commercial instrument and penalty catalogues beyond the terms that bind a planned intention
Goal, objective, benefit and requirement catalogues as standing definitions
Care-condition, diagnosis and clinical-order catalogues; FHIR CarePlan is aligned only as an intention-of-care projection
Manufacturing MRP, MES and ISA-95 operations-schedule engines
Automated planner search, PDDL domains, HTN methods and solver traces
Shift rostering, crew pairing, court calendars, legislative calendars and military operation orders as specialised industry models
Interface, storage and encoding concerns: JSON, YAML, ICS, CalDAV, MCP, MongoDB, Git

boundary_notes.neighbor: Act or action sibling (recorded completed acts)
boundary_notes.distinction: Intention is a distinct mode of fact: neither a completed act nor a standing definition. Divergence of a plan from later acts is essential information and is expressed by reference to the act sibling, not by storing performance inside this model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Aligned external standards (iCalendar, JSCalendar, PROV Plan, P-Plan, FHIR CarePlan, OWL-Time, ISO 21502)
boundary_notes.distinction: These specifications are alignments; this model does not claim conformance to any one of them.
FHIR CarePlan represents a specific patient or group instance, not a generic protocol (that is PlanDefinition).

boundary_notes.neighbor: PROV Plan as a standalone provenance term
boundary_notes.distinction: PROV Plan is an entity associated with an activity and does not by itself define recurrence or free-busy.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Named PMI or ISO schedule baseline
boundary_notes.distinction: iCalendar SEQUENCE is an organizer revision counter, not a named PMI or ISO schedule baseline.
Calendar sharing protocols are interfaces, not semantics.
Resource assignment and working-time calendars as HR or plant-capacity objects belong in sibling resource and calendar-of-record models; only the availability projection of a plan is in scope.

sources.title: RFC 5545: Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification (iCalendar)
sources.relevance: Primary calendaring object specification; aligned for calendar component, recurrence, free-busy, classification, attendee and identity properties. Recurrence expansion ambiguities are recorded as conflicts, not hidden.

sources.title: RFC 5546: iCalendar Transport-Independent Interoperability Protocol (iTIP)
sources.relevance: Application protocol for group scheduling independent of transport; source of scheduling methods, organizer and attendee workflow, SEQUENCE rules and message ordering.

sources.title: RFC 8984: JSCalendar: A JSON Representation of Calendar Data
sources.relevance: IETF JSON calendar data model and the source of this-and-future split semantics and clarified recurrence; aligned for Event, Task, Group, LocalDateTime, timeZone, recurrenceOverrides, relatedTo and RFC 3339 UTCDateTime.

sources.title: RFC 9253: Support for iCalendar Relationships
sources.relevance: Primary source for project-style temporal relations on calendar components: precedence types, GAP lead and lag, REFID grouping and LINK.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Defines Plan as an entity and the association hadPlan; aligned for attribution, revision, generation and invalidation of plan versions.

sources.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
sources.relevance: Defines Plan as actions or steps intended by agents to achieve goals but leaves step structure to extensions; aligned for plan-as-entity, revision, generation and invalidation.

sources.title: Time Ontology in OWL
sources.relevance: Primary temporal topology vocabulary and the source of non-Gregorian TRS support beyond CALSCALE; aligned for Instant, ProperInterval, duration and Allen interval relations.

sources.title: The P-PLAN Ontology
sources.organization: Ontology Engineering Group, Universidad Politecnica de Madrid, and Information Sciences Institute, University of Southern California
sources.relevance: Primary scientific extension that structures plans into Steps and Variables and links them to execution traces; aligned for isPreceededBy, correspondsToStep and correspondsToVariable.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR CarePlan (Release 4)
sources.relevance: Primary instance-level care-intention resource; aligned for status and intent strength, partOf, basedOn, replaces and activity references. PlanDefinition remains out of scope.

sources.title: ISO 21502:2020 Project, programme and portfolio management - Guidance on project management
sources.relevance: Catalogue-level guidance treating schedule as structuring work, estimating durations, sequencing activities and maintaining a credible schedule baseline. Full text is paywalled, so baseline naming is an alignment with an evidence gap.

bundles.name: Intention
bundles.description: What is intended, by whom, with what authority and under which assumptions, independent of a particular clock binding.
bundles.rationale: Plan identity and lifecycle, planned content and commitment are grouped because each holds independently of any clock binding; separating them from Timing keeps what is intended distinct from when it is bound.

layers.name: Plan identity and lifecycle
layers.description: Identify a plan as a governed entity and record how firmly and in which lifecycle state the intention currently stands.

findings.name: Plan master identity
findings.description: A plan is an identifiable entity representing a set of intended actions or steps. Persistent identity is a globally unique identifier on the plan object (iCalendar UID, JSCalendar uid, FHIR CarePlan.identifier or logical id, PROV entity id). An occurrence of a recurring plan item is not a new master identity: it is the master identifier qualified by a recurrence identifier. A date, horizon or freeze time is not an identifier.

data_elements.name: master_system_id
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the authoritative calendar, EHR, planner or project-scheduling system of record.

data_elements.name: global_uid
data_elements.description: Persistent globally unique identifier (iCalendar UID or JSCalendar uid); UUID version 4 is recommended by JSCalendar.

data_elements.name: governed_iri
data_elements.description: Governed IRI for the plan as a PROV Entity or FHIR canonical or business identifier.

data_elements.name: dimension_ulid
data_elements.description: ULID or UUID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master-system or governed IRI exists.

data_elements.name: title
data_elements.description: Human-readable name or JSCalendar title or FHIR CarePlan.title or iCalendar SUMMARY.

data_elements.name: prod_id
data_elements.description: Product identifier of the last updating implementation (JSCalendar prodId, iCalendar PRODID).

artifacts.name: Plan record
artifacts.description: Governed plan object carrying master identity, title, locale and product stamp, independent of any one file encoding.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system identifier where one exists, else the global UID or uid, else a governed IRI, else a Dimension-assigned ULID; a date is never used as the identifier.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this plan, and which governed IRI or Dimension ULID is used when the master system is absent or federated?
Is the same UID or uid reused across systems to mean the same plan, and is it large enough to persist at least 255 octets without truncation inside a UTF-8 sequence?
What title, locale and product identifier should agents use when referring to this plan in human and machine interchange?

findings.name: Plan status and intent strength
findings.description: A plan has a lifecycle status distinct from the strength of authority that backs it. FHIR CarePlan.status is draft, active, on-hold, revoked, completed, entered-in-error or unknown, and CarePlan.intent is proposal, plan, order or option. iCalendar STATUS for events is tentative, confirmed or cancelled; for to-dos includes needs-action, in-process and completed. JSCalendar Event status is confirmed, cancelled or tentative. These vocabularies overlap but do not coincide: a FHIR proposal is not an iCalendar tentative event, and cancelled is not the same as revoked or deleted.

data_elements.name: lifecycle_status
data_elements.description: Union status: draft, tentative, active or confirmed, on-hold, in-process, completed, cancelled, revoked, entered-in-error, unknown.

data_elements.name: intent_strength
data_elements.description: Authority of the intention: proposal, plan, order or option as in FHIR CarePlan.intent.

data_elements.name: status_vocabulary
data_elements.description: Which aligned vocabulary is the source of the stored code and how it maps to the union.

data_elements.name: percent_complete
data_elements.description: Optional iCalendar PERCENT-COMPLETE for to-do style planned items, 0 to 100.

artifacts.name: Plan status record
artifacts.description: Current lifecycle status and intent-strength pair with vocabulary mapping, stored with the plan rather than inferred from dates.
media_or_form: Status and intent code pair with its source vocabulary mapping
artifacts.identity_strategy: Held against the owning plan identifier together with the vocabulary that supplied the stored code.

questions.text: Which lifecycle status does this plan currently hold, and which aligned vocabulary supplied that code?
Is this intention a proposal, a plan the agent currently holds, a binding order, or an option in a larger plan?
If the plan or planned item reports progress toward completion, what percent-complete or completed flag is asserted, and is that a statement of intention status rather than a recorded act?

layers.name: Planned content
layers.description: Describe the intended steps, their inputs and outputs, and the assumptions the plan depends on.

findings.name: Planned step or action
findings.description: A plan is composed of steps. P-Plan models a Plan as Steps that use and produce Variables; a Step may itself be a Plan. JSCalendar distinguishes Event (scheduled time with duration) from Task (action item that may have start, due and estimated duration). FHIR CarePlan.activity holds intended actions, either inline or by reference to a request resource. iCalendar VEVENT and VTODO are calendar projections of those intended items, not standing process definitions. Expected effort, priority and description live on the planned step. Realization by later acts is a relationship out to the act sibling.

data_elements.name: step_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the planned step within the plan.

data_elements.name: intended_verb
data_elements.description: Intended action or activity type.

data_elements.name: target_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to the intended object, patient, deliverable or variable.

data_elements.name: priority
data_elements.description: iCalendar PRIORITY 0-9 or JSCalendar priority 0-9; 0 means undefined.

data_elements.name: estimated_duration
data_elements.description: Expected effort or JSCalendar estimatedDuration for a Task.

data_elements.name: input_variable_ids
data_elements.description: P-Plan input variables of the step.

data_elements.name: output_variable_ids
data_elements.description: P-Plan output variables of the step.

data_elements.name: instantiates_definition_ref
data_elements.description: Optional reference to a process or PlanDefinition sibling this instance instantiates (FHIR instantiatesCanonical).

artifacts.name: Planned step record
artifacts.description: One intended action or step with verb, target, priority, estimated duration and planned inputs and outputs.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Step identifier scoped to the owning plan identifier; a nested step that is itself a plan carries its own plan identity.

questions.text: Which planned steps does this plan contain, and is any step itself a nested plan?
What intended verb, target, priority and estimated duration describe this planned step?
Which planned input and output variables must exist for this step to be executable as intended, and which standing process definition if any does the step instantiate?
Which recorded acts, if any, are asserted to correspond to this planned step, without storing those acts in this model?

findings.name: Assumptions and planning constraints
findings.description: A plan depends on conditions that are not themselves scheduled actions. FHIR CarePlan can be tied to Conditions and can carry activity detail including status and doNotPerform. iCalendar encodes some constraints as property restrictions (DTEND exclusive of DURATION; UNTIL type matching DTSTART). OWL-Time records temporal constraints among intervals. Sensitivity of the plan to an assumption and a monitoring signal are operational fields this model must hold because they explain later divergence, but they are not standardised as a single primary class; they are recorded as plan-scoped condition statements with provenance.

data_elements.name: assumption_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the assumption or constraint statement.

data_elements.name: statement
data_elements.description: Condition the plan relies on.

data_elements.name: kind
data_elements.description: assumption, precondition, exclusion, temporal-constraint or do-not-perform.

data_elements.name: sensitivity
data_elements.description: How severely a false assumption would invalidate the plan: low, medium, high.

data_elements.name: monitoring_signal_ref
data_elements.description: Signal, observation or condition reference used to watch the assumption.

data_elements.name: related_condition_ref
data_elements.description: Optional FHIR Condition or equivalent clinical or operational condition.

artifacts.name: Plan assumption record
artifacts.description: A condition statement the plan relies on, with kind, sensitivity and monitoring signal, stored with the plan.
media_or_form: FHIR CarePlan activity detail or Condition reference
artifacts.identity_strategy: Assumption identifier scoped to the owning plan identifier; referenced conditions keep their own sibling identity.

questions.text: What conditions does this plan rely on, and is each an assumption, precondition, exclusion or do-not-perform instruction?
How sensitive is the plan to this assumption being false, and what signal is monitored to detect that?
Does this assumption reference a condition, observation or other sibling-model entity that lives outside the plan?

layers.name: Commitment
layers.description: Record promises that bind agents to intended items, including calendar participation as a specialised commitment surface.

findings.name: Binding commitment and participation obligation
findings.description: Some intentions become binding relative to another party. iTIP models this as Organizer-initiated REQUEST and Attendee REPLY with PARTSTAT needs-action, accepted, declined, tentative, delegated or completed. ROLE and RSVP parameters describe required versus optional participation. FHIR CarePlan.intent of order is stronger than plan or proposal. A full commercial contract is out of scope; the commitment object here is the binding of an agent to a planned item with terms, beneficiary and optional penalty or remedy stated on that binding. Delegation (DELEGATED-TO, DELEGATED-FROM, SENT-BY) transfers attendance, not ownership of the master object; the Organizer retains the master.

data_elements.name: commitment_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the binding.

data_elements.name: planned_item_id
data_elements.description: Plan or planned step being bound.

data_elements.name: committing_agent_id
data_elements.description: Agent making the promise or accepting participation.

data_elements.name: beneficiary_agent_id
data_elements.description: Party to whom the commitment is made; often the Organizer.

data_elements.name: participation_status
data_elements.description: needs-action, accepted, declined, tentative, delegated, completed.

data_elements.name: participation_role
data_elements.description: chair, required participant, optional participant, non-participant, information-only.

data_elements.name: rsvp_expected
data_elements.description: Whether a reply is required.

data_elements.name: terms
data_elements.description: Binding terms specific to this intention.

data_elements.name: penalty_or_remedy
data_elements.description: Stated consequence or remedy if the commitment is broken; not a full legal instrument.

artifacts.name: Commitment record
artifacts.description: Binding of a committing agent to a planned item, including participation status, role, RSVP flag and stated terms.
media_or_form: iTIP REQUEST and REPLY participation record
Stated terms attached to the binding
artifacts.identity_strategy: Commitment identifier scoped to the planned item identifier and the committing agent; delegation records the delegate without changing the master owner.

questions.text: Which agent commits, which agent or party is the beneficiary, and which planned item is bound?
What is the current participation or honouring status of this commitment, and is a reply still expected?
What terms, role and penalty or remedy make this intention binding, as distinct from a mere personal plan?
Has participation been delegated, and if so to whom and with what SENT-BY or acting-on-behalf agent remaining responsible?

bundles.name: Timing
bundles.description: Bind intentions to instants, intervals, recurrences, time zones and availability projections.
bundles.rationale: Schedule interval, recurrence and time zone or availability are grouped because each is a clock binding applied to an intention, and a free-busy view is a reduced projection of those same bindings rather than a separate plan.

layers.name: Schedule interval
layers.description: Fix a planned item to a start, end or due instant or interval, including floating time and all-day presentations.

findings.name: Schedule entry time binding
findings.description: A schedule entry binds a planned item to time. iCalendar uses DTSTART with optional DTEND or DURATION (mutually exclusive) and DUE for to-dos; DATE versus DATE-TIME distinguishes all-day from timed values. JSCalendar uses start as LocalDateTime, duration, timeZone, showWithoutTime and, for tasks, due. OWL-Time supplies Instant, ProperInterval, hasBeginning, hasEnd and hasTemporalDuration. JSCalendar UTCDateTime is RFC 3339 date-time with seconds, uppercase letters and offset Z. Event time (start, end, due) is not the same as created, updated or DTSTAMP observation time.

data_elements.name: entry_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the schedule entry.

data_elements.name: planned_item_id
data_elements.description: Planned step or event this entry times.

data_elements.name: start_local
data_elements.description: Local start without offset; interpreted with time_zone or as floating.

data_elements.name: start_utc
data_elements.description: Start as UTC instant when zoned; RFC 3339 with seconds and Z or numeric offset.

data_elements.name: end_local
data_elements.description: Local end; iCalendar DTEND is exclusive of DATE values.

data_elements.name: duration
data_elements.description: Positive duration; must not be stored together with an explicit end in iCalendar.

data_elements.name: due_local
data_elements.description: Due instant for task-like items.

data_elements.name: show_without_time
data_elements.description: All-day or date-only presentation; time still used for free-busy.

data_elements.name: time_zone_id
data_elements.description: IANA Time Zone Database identifier or null for floating time.

data_elements.name: flexibility
data_elements.description: fixed, window, or as-soon-as-predecessor-allows.

data_elements.name: location_ref
data_elements.description: Occurrence location reference; location master data is a sibling.

artifacts.name: Schedule entry
artifacts.description: Time binding for a planned item, including start, end or duration, due, zone and all-day flag.
media_or_form: iCalendar DTSTART with DTEND or DURATION and DUE
JSCalendar start, duration, timeZone and showWithoutTime
artifacts.identity_strategy: Entry identifier bound to the planned item identifier; for a recurring master, the master identifier qualified by a recurrence identifier rather than by a bare date.

questions.text: When is this planned item intended to start and end or fall due, in local civil time and as a UTC instant, and is duration used instead of an explicit end?
Is the binding floating (no time zone), zoned, or show-without-time, and how should free-busy treat that interval?
Where is the occurrence intended to take place, including distinct start and end locations when travel crosses zones?
What is the intended event time versus the created, updated or DTSTAMP observation or ingestion time of this entry?

layers.name: Recurrence
layers.description: Generate, exclude and override repeating occurrences from a master planned item.

findings.name: Recurrence rules, exceptions and overrides
findings.description: A recurrence rule generates extra date-times from a master start or due. iCalendar RRULE uses FREQ, INTERVAL, UNTIL or COUNT, WKST and BY* parts; RDATE adds dates; EXDATE excludes them; RECURRENCE-ID identifies one instance. JSCalendar applies recurrenceRules, then excludedRecurrenceRules, then recurrenceOverrides as PatchObject diffs, and uses rscale (default gregorian) and skip from RFC 7529. Multiple rules are unioned. JSCalendar documents that RFC 5545 recurrence expansion has been ambiguous across implementations; this model stores the rule plus materialised or overridden instances rather than claiming a single expansion algorithm. UNTIL type must match DTSTART, and zoned UNTIL is UTC.

data_elements.name: frequency
data_elements.description: yearly, monthly, weekly, daily, hourly, minutely, secondly.

data_elements.name: interval
data_elements.description: Positive integer iteration interval, default 1.

data_elements.name: until
data_elements.description: Inclusive end of recurrence; type-matched to start; UTC when start is zoned.

data_elements.name: count
data_elements.description: Occurrence cap; mutually exclusive with until.

data_elements.name: by_parts
data_elements.description: BYDAY, BYMONTHDAY, BYMONTH, BYYEARDAY, BYWEEKNO, BYHOUR, BYMINUTE, BYSECOND, BYSETPOS.

data_elements.name: rscale
data_elements.description: CLDR calendar system, default gregorian.

data_elements.name: skip
data_elements.description: omit, backward or forward when an expansion is an invalid date.

data_elements.name: excluded_dates
data_elements.description: Exception dates removed from the generated set.

data_elements.name: added_dates
data_elements.description: Additional recurrence dates.

data_elements.name: overrides
data_elements.description: Per-occurrence patches keyed by recurrence id.

artifacts.name: Recurrence rule set
artifacts.description: Rule, excluded-rule, added dates, excluded dates and occurrence overrides that generate the recurrence set of a master item.
media_or_form: iCalendar RRULE, RDATE and EXDATE properties
artifacts.identity_strategy: Held against the master item identifier; an individual occurrence is qualified by its recurrence identifier and never by a bare date used as a surrogate key.

questions.text: What frequency, interval, by-parts, until or count, rscale and skip behaviour generate this recurrence set?
Which dates are excluded or additionally included, and which occurrence overrides patch individual instances?
For a materialised occurrence, what recurrence identifier combined with the master UID identifies that instance, and is this a this-and-future split rather than a single-instance override?
Which expansion profile (iCalendar RRULE, JSCalendar recurrenceRules, or a named engine) is authoritative, given known ambiguities in RFC 5545 expansion?

layers.name: Time zone and availability
layers.description: Interpret civil times against a zone or temporal reference system and project busy or free intervals.

findings.name: Time zone, calendar scale and free-busy projection
findings.description: Zoned local times require a time zone identifier (IANA TZDB or iCalendar VTIMEZONE). JSCalendar specifies conversion across DST discontinuities: use the offset before the transition; leap seconds are not considered. OWL-Time supports non-Gregorian TRS, while iCalendar CALSCALE defaults to GREGORIAN. Free-busy is a reduced projection: iCalendar VFREEBUSY and FREEBUSY with FBTYPE free, busy, busy-unavailable or busy-tentative; TRANSP opaque or transparent; iTIP can PUBLISH or REQUEST busy time. A free-busy view omits plan content. Working calendars and VAVAILABILITY (RFC 7953) are not in the fetched primary set and are a known omission.

data_elements.name: time_zone_id
data_elements.description: IANA TZDB name or custom zone identifier.

data_elements.name: calendar_scale
data_elements.description: CALSCALE or OWL-Time TRS; default Gregorian.

data_elements.name: transparency
data_elements.description: opaque or transparent for busy calculation.

data_elements.name: freebusy_type
data_elements.description: free, busy, busy-unavailable, busy-tentative.

data_elements.name: freebusy_period_start
data_elements.description: Start of a busy or free period in UTC.

data_elements.name: freebusy_period_end
data_elements.description: End of that period in UTC.

data_elements.name: horizon_start
data_elements.description: Start of the availability horizon being disclosed.

data_elements.name: horizon_end
data_elements.description: End of the availability horizon being disclosed.

artifacts.name: Free-busy document
artifacts.description: Reduced availability projection over a horizon, omitting plan content, with busy type and periods.
media_or_form: iTIP PUBLISH or REQUEST of busy time
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the owning calendar user or agent plus the disclosed horizon start and end; plan content is omitted from the projection.

questions.text: Which time zone or temporal reference system interprets this local time, and which offset applies if the local time falls in a DST discontinuity?
Over which horizon may a consumer read free-busy rather than full entries, and which periods are free, busy, tentative or unavailable?
Does this entry block the calendar (opaque) or leave the interval free for other scheduling (transparent)?

bundles.name: Coordination
bundles.description: Order planned items, relate them hierarchically, and exchange scheduling messages among organizers and attendees.
bundles.rationale: Precedence and hierarchy, participation and scheduling exchange are grouped because each concerns more than one planned item or more than one agent, and RFC 9253 and iTIP supply the primary vocabulary for those relations and exchanges.

layers.name: Precedence and hierarchy
layers.description: Capture ordering constraints and parent-child structure among planned items.

findings.name: Precedence network and hierarchical composition
findings.description: RFC 9253 extends RELATED-TO with temporal RELTYPE values FINISHTOSTART, FINISHTOFINISH, STARTTOFINISH and STARTTOSTART, plus GAP for lag (positive) or lead (negative) duration, and FIRST, NEXT, DEPENDS-ON, PARENT, CHILD and SIBLING. P-Plan isPreceededBy is a transitive step ordering without lag types. OWL-Time intervalBefore, intervalMeets, intervalOverlaps and related Allen relations describe interval topology but are not project-management lag. FHIR CarePlan.partOf, basedOn and replaces relate plan instances. REFID groups components without adding meaning. These relation families must be stored distinctly; isPreceededBy is not equivalent to FINISHTOSTART with lag.

data_elements.name: predecessor_id
data_elements.description: Planned item that constrains another.

data_elements.name: successor_id
data_elements.description: Planned item being constrained.

data_elements.name: reltype
data_elements.description: finishtostart, finishtofinish, starttofinish, starttostart, depends-on, parent, child, sibling, first, next, part-of, based-on, replaces.

data_elements.name: gap
data_elements.description: Lead (negative) or lag (positive) between predecessor and successor.

data_elements.name: group_refid
data_elements.description: Shared grouping key with no additional semantics.

data_elements.name: link_uri
data_elements.description: RFC 9253 LINK to an external related resource.

artifacts.name: Dependency record
artifacts.description: Typed relationship between planned items, including precedence type, gap and optional grouping key.
media_or_form: iCalendar RELATED-TO with RELTYPE and GAP
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by predecessor identifier, successor identifier and relation type; relation families are stored distinctly rather than collapsed together.

questions.text: What ordering constraint holds between these planned items, including precedence type and lead or lag gap?
Is this plan or item part of, based on, replacing, parent of or child of another plan, and what grouping REFID if any associates peers?
Independently of project lag, which Allen interval relation holds between the scheduled intervals of the two items?
Does this relationship currently dangle because the target was deleted or cancelled, as RFC 9253 warns for FIRST, NEXT and temporal links?

layers.name: Participation
layers.description: Identify organizer and attendee roles on a scheduled item.

findings.name: Organizer and attendee roles
findings.description: iTIP distinguishes Organizer (initiates and owns the master object) from Attendee (recipient who replies). ROLE on ATTENDEE is descriptive (chair, required, optional) and is not the Organizer workflow role. CUTYPE classifies the calendar user as individual, group, resource, room or unknown. JSCalendar participants are a map of participant objects. Attendees do not directly mutate the master; they REPLY or COUNTER. SENT-BY records that another calendar user acted on behalf of the Organizer or Attendee. Resource and room CUTYPE values are participation classifications, not resource master data.

data_elements.name: organizer_agent_id
data_elements.description: Calendar user who owns the master scheduling object.

data_elements.name: attendee_agent_id
data_elements.description: Invited calendar user.

data_elements.name: calendar_user_type
data_elements.description: individual, group, resource, room, unknown.

data_elements.name: calendar_address
data_elements.description: mailto or other calendar user address.

data_elements.name: common_name
data_elements.description: Display name (CN).

data_elements.name: sent_by_agent_id
data_elements.description: Agent who acted on behalf of organizer or attendee.

artifacts.name: Participant record
artifacts.description: Organizer or attendee participation on a scheduled item, with calendar user type and address.
media_or_form: iCalendar ORGANIZER and ATTENDEE properties with CUTYPE, ROLE and CN
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by calendar user address within the owning scheduling object; person or organization master identity remains in the sibling model.

questions.text: Who is the Organizer of the master object, and did another user send on that Organizer's behalf?
Which attendees are invited, with what calendar-user type and descriptive role, and are any of them rooms or resources rather than persons?
What calendar address and common name identify this participant, and which person or organization sibling do they reference?

layers.name: Scheduling exchange
layers.description: Describe the methods and sequencing rules used to publish, request, update and cancel scheduled items.

findings.name: Scheduling methods and message sequencing
findings.description: iTIP methods are PUBLISH, REQUEST, REPLY, ADD, CANCEL, REFRESH, COUNTER and DECLINECOUNTER. Organizer may send PUBLISH, REQUEST, ADD, CANCEL and DECLINECOUNTER; Attendee may send REPLY, REFRESH, COUNTER and a delegation REQUEST. Correlation keys are UID, RECURRENCE-ID, SEQUENCE and DTSTAMP: higher SEQUENCE obsoletes lower for the same UID and recurrence id; matching SEQUENCE ties break on later DTSTAMP. SEQUENCE MUST increment when Organizer changes DTSTART, DTEND, DURATION, DUE, RRULE, RDATE, EXDATE or STATUS. JSCalendar sequence and method (lowercase iTIP method) carry the same semantics. Out-of-order replies must be discarded using persisted last SEQUENCE and DTSTAMP per attendee.

data_elements.name: method
data_elements.description: publish, request, reply, add, cancel, refresh, counter, declinecounter.

data_elements.name: sequence
data_elements.description: Organizer revision number, starting at 0.

data_elements.name: stamp_time
data_elements.description: DTSTAMP or JSCalendar updated used as sequencing tie-breaker.

data_elements.name: originator_role
data_elements.description: organizer or attendee.

data_elements.name: request_status
data_elements.description: iTIP REQUEST-STATUS machine-readable result.

artifacts.name: Scheduling message
artifacts.description: One iTIP-style method payload correlated by UID, recurrence id, sequence and stamp time.
media_or_form: iTIP method payload (PUBLISH, REQUEST, REPLY, ADD, CANCEL, REFRESH, COUNTER, DECLINECOUNTER)
JSCalendar object carrying method and sequence
artifacts.identity_strategy: Correlated by UID plus recurrence identifier plus SEQUENCE, with the later stamp time breaking equal-sequence ties; a higher sequence obsoletes a lower one for the same pair.

questions.text: Which scheduling method is being applied, who may send it, and is this a new object or a revision of an existing UID?
What SEQUENCE and stamp time identify this revision, and does it obsolete a previously stored component with the same UID and recurrence id?
If a reply arrives with a lower sequence or earlier stamp than the last persisted attendee response, should it be discarded?
What spoofing, unauthorized organizer-replacement or flood controls apply to this scheduling message, as warned in iTIP security considerations?

bundles.name: Revision and governance
bundles.description: Freeze baselines, record plan provenance and realization correspondence, and govern classification, sharing, retention and deletion.
bundles.rationale: Baselines, provenance and disclosure are grouped because each governs a plan version over time: what was frozen for comparison, how the version was produced and revised, and who may read or must retain it.

layers.name: Baseline and version
layers.description: Identify frozen comparison snapshots and this-and-future splits.

findings.name: Schedule baseline and this-and-future split
findings.description: ISO 21502 guidance treats schedule as structuring work, estimating durations, sequencing activities and maintaining a credible schedule baseline. iCalendar and JSCalendar have no named baseline object: they have SEQUENCE plus created and updated timestamps. A baseline in this model is therefore an explicit frozen snapshot of a plan (a PROV Entity, often a Bundle of descriptions) with freeze time and approver, used later to compare intention with performance. JSCalendar this-and-future changes truncate the original series and create a new object linked by relatedTo next and first. That split is a new master identity, not a baseline. Claiming that SEQUENCE equals a PMI or ISO baseline is a conflict, not a conformance.

data_elements.name: baseline_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the frozen snapshot.

data_elements.name: baseline_name
data_elements.description: Human name of the baseline.

data_elements.name: freezes_plan_id
data_elements.description: Plan whose state was frozen.

data_elements.name: freeze_time
data_elements.description: Event time the baseline was approved; not used as an identifier.

data_elements.name: approver_agent_id
data_elements.description: Agent who approved the freeze.

data_elements.name: snapshot_bundle_ref
data_elements.description: PROV Bundle or equivalent snapshot of plan descriptions.

data_elements.name: split_next_uid
data_elements.description: UID of the successor object after a this-and-future split.

data_elements.name: split_first_uid
data_elements.description: UID of the first object in the split series.

artifacts.name: Baseline snapshot
artifacts.description: Named frozen copy of a plan used as the comparison basis for later variance, with approver and freeze time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Baseline identifier and name held against the frozen plan identifier; freeze time is recorded as event time but is never the identifier, and a SEQUENCE increment alone does not create one.

questions.text: Which named baseline freezes this plan, who approved it, and at what freeze time?
Against which baseline should current schedule entries and realized acts be compared, and what planned start, end and duration were frozen?
If a this-and-future change split the series, which UIDs are linked as first and next, and which object was truncated?
Is this snapshot an explicit named baseline, or only an iTIP SEQUENCE increment, and has anyone treated SEQUENCE as if it were an ISO schedule baseline?

layers.name: Provenance and realization
layers.description: Record how the plan was produced, revised and later corresponded to execution.

findings.name: Plan provenance and correspondence to execution
findings.description: A PROV Plan is an entity representing actions or steps intended by agents to achieve goals, associated with an activity via hadPlan. P-Plan adds Step and Variable structure and links execution: a p-plan:Activity correspondsToStep a p-plan:Step, and a p-plan:Entity correspondsToVariable. Plans themselves have provenance: wasRevisionOf, generatedAtTime, invalidatedAtTime, wasAttributedTo. Execution correspondence is many-to-one from acts to a planned step and may be missing when a step is skipped or fails. This model stores the correspondence reference; the act remains in the act sibling.

data_elements.name: plan_entity_id
data_elements.description: PROV Entity id of the plan.

data_elements.name: planning_agent_id
data_elements.description: Agent associated with or attributed for the plan.

data_elements.name: had_plan_activity_id
data_elements.description: Activity that used this plan.

data_elements.name: revision_of_plan_id
data_elements.description: Previous plan entity this one revises.

data_elements.name: generated_at
data_elements.description: Generation time of this plan version.

data_elements.name: invalidated_at
data_elements.description: Time this plan version ceased to be the current intention.

data_elements.name: execution_activity_id
data_elements.description: P-Plan activity that corresponds to a step.

data_elements.name: corresponds_to_step_id
data_elements.description: Planned step the execution activity claims to follow.

artifacts.name: Plan provenance record
artifacts.description: Attribution, revision, generation and invalidation of a plan version, plus optional correspondence of an execution activity to a planned step.
media_or_form: PROV-O attribution, revision, generation and invalidation assertions
artifacts.identity_strategy: Plan entity IRI for the version, linked to the prior entity it revises; correspondence is stored as a reference while the act stays in the act sibling.

questions.text: Which agent is attributed with this plan version, which activity had this plan, and at what generation time was this version created?
Which prior plan entity is this a revision of, and when was the prior version invalidated as current intention?
Which execution activities correspond to which planned steps, and which steps have no corresponding activity (skipped, failed or not yet started)?
Where a corresponding act exists, what signed difference in start, end or duration is observed relative to the planned entry or baseline, without copying the act into this model?

layers.name: Disclosure, access and retention
layers.description: Classify plan content, project reduced views, and distinguish cancel from delete.

findings.name: Classification, sharing projections and retention
findings.description: iCalendar CLASS is public, private or confidential (default public). JSCalendar privacy is public, private or secret. Free-busy and agenda or Gantt projections are reduced views, not separate plans. FHIR CarePlan is Patient-security-categorised. iTIP CANCEL sets STATUS cancelled and increments SEQUENCE; it is not a silent delete. FHIR revoked and entered-in-error are distinct from completed. PROV invalidatedAtTime records when a plan version ceased to be usable. Retention of cancelled or revoked plans is required for audit of commitments and of divergence from acts. Calendar sharing is an access grant over entries at an agreed detail level and horizon, not a change of ownership. The planning agent owns the plan; beneficiaries hold verification rights over commitments made to them.

data_elements.name: classification
data_elements.description: public, private, confidential or secret.

data_elements.name: owner_agent_id
data_elements.description: Planning agent who owns the plan.

data_elements.name: share_detail_level
data_elements.description: full, agenda, gantt, freebusy or none.

data_elements.name: share_horizon_end
data_elements.description: Latest time a grantee may read.

data_elements.name: grantee_agent_id
data_elements.description: Agent granted a projection.

data_elements.name: retention_action
data_elements.description: keep-cancelled, revoke, mark-entered-in-error, invalidate, or purge after policy.

data_elements.name: invalidated_at
data_elements.description: Time the plan version was invalidated or cancelled as current intention.

artifacts.name: Calendar share grant
artifacts.description: Access grant naming grantee, detail level, horizon and classification, without transferring ownership.
media_or_form: Access grant naming grantee, detail level, horizon and classification
iCalendar CLASS or JSCalendar privacy value applied to the projection
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by grantee agent identifier plus the granted plan or projection and its horizon; ownership stays with the planning agent.

questions.text: Which planning agent owns this plan, and which beneficiaries hold verification rights over commitments made to them?
Who may read which projection of this plan (full, agenda, gantt or free-busy), at what classification and through which horizon?
Is this plan or entry cancelled, revoked, entered-in-error, invalidated or actually purged, and must the cancelled record be retained for commitment audit?
What emergency, legal-hold or clinical break-glass exception, if any, overrides the default owner-grant rule, and what audit record is required?

functions.name: Adopt plan
functions.description: Accept a draft or proposed plan as the current intention of the planning agent, setting lifecycle status to active or confirmed and recording generation time and attribution.
outputs: Plan whose lifecycle status is active or confirmed
preconditions: A draft or proposed plan exists
effects: Lifecycle status set to active or confirmed
Generation time and attribution recorded against the plan version

functions.name: Bind commitment
functions.description: Create a binding of a committing agent to a planned item, typically by Organizer REQUEST with ATTENDEE RSVP, setting participation status to needs-action until reply.
outputs: Commitment record with participation status needs-action
preconditions: An Organizer holds the master scheduling object
effects: Organizer REQUEST issued with ATTENDEE RSVP
Participation status set to needs-action until a reply arrives

functions.name: Reply participation
functions.description: Attendee updates PARTSTAT to accepted, declined, tentative, delegated or completed and returns a REPLY correlated by UID, recurrence id, sequence and stamp time.
inputs: Scheduling REQUEST addressed to the attendee
outputs: REPLY message carrying the updated participation status
preconditions: The replying agent is an Attendee of the master object
effects: PARTSTAT updated to accepted, declined, tentative, delegated or completed
REPLY correlated by UID, recurrence id, sequence and stamp time

functions.name: Schedule entry
functions.description: Bind a planned item to start, end or due, duration, time zone and show-without-time, recording event time separately from created and updated observation times.
outputs: Schedule entry with start, end or due, duration, time zone and show-without-time
preconditions: A planned item exists to be timed
effects: Time binding attached to the planned item
Event time recorded separately from created and updated observation times

functions.name: Expand recurrence
functions.description: Apply recurrence rules, excluded rules, added dates, excluded dates and overrides to produce the occurrence set, using a named expansion profile because RFC 5545 expansion is known-ambiguous.
inputs: Master item with recurrence rules, excluded rules, added dates, excluded dates and overrides
outputs: Occurrence set generated from the master item
preconditions: An expansion profile is named, because RFC 5545 recurrence expansion is known-ambiguous
effects: Rules, exclusions, additions and overrides applied to produce the occurrence set
Occurrences remain qualified by master identifier plus recurrence identifier

functions.name: Shift schedule
functions.description: Move a time binding and increment SEQUENCE when DTSTART, DTEND, DURATION, DUE or recurrence properties change, persisting the reason and the new stamp time.
outputs: Revised entry with an incremented sequence and a new stamp time
preconditions: The acting agent is the Organizer of the master object
effects: Time binding moved
SEQUENCE incremented when DTSTART, DTEND, DURATION, DUE or recurrence properties change
Reason and new stamp time persisted

functions.name: Freeze baseline
functions.description: Create a named frozen snapshot of the current plan for later comparison, with approver and freeze time; do not treat a mere SEQUENCE increment as a named baseline.
outputs: Named baseline snapshot carrying approver and freeze time
effects: Frozen snapshot created as the comparison basis for later variance
A mere SEQUENCE increment is not treated as a named baseline

functions.name: Cancel or abandon
functions.description: Cancel one or more instances or abandon a plan using CANCEL or status cancelled, revoked or invalidated, retaining the record for audit rather than silent purge.
inputs: Plan or one or more of its instances
outputs: Cancelled, revoked or invalidated record retained for audit
preconditions: The acting agent owns the plan or holds the master scheduling object
effects: CANCEL issued or status set to cancelled, revoked or invalidated
Record retained for audit rather than silently purged

functions.name: Publish free-busy
functions.description: Disclose an availability projection over a horizon without revealing plan content, using free, busy, busy-tentative and busy-unavailable periods.
outputs: Availability projection of free, busy, busy-tentative and busy-unavailable periods
preconditions: A disclosure horizon and grant are in place
effects: Availability disclosed over the stated horizon
Plan content withheld from the projection

functions.name: Compare intention to execution
functions.description: Link execution activities to planned steps via correspondsToStep and compute signed time variance against the planned entry or a named baseline, leaving acts in the act sibling.
inputs: Planned steps or a named baseline
outputs: Signed time variance against the planned entry or named baseline
preconditions: Execution activities are linked to planned steps via correspondsToStep
effects: Execution activities linked to the planned steps they claim to follow
Acts remain stored in the act sibling rather than copied into the plan

functions.name: Split this-and-future
functions.description: Truncate a recurring master at the previous occurrence and create a new master for future occurrences, linking the objects with first and next relations.
outputs: Truncated original master and a new master covering future occurrences
preconditions: The item is a recurring master with occurrences after the split point
effects: Original series truncated at the previous occurrence
New master created with its own identity and linked by first and next relations

functions.name: Counter proposal
functions.description: Attendee proposes a change via COUNTER; Organizer accepts by a new REQUEST or refuses via DECLINECOUNTER without transferring master ownership.
inputs: Attendee-proposed change to a scheduled item
outputs: COUNTER message and the Organizer's REQUEST or DECLINECOUNTER response
preconditions: The proposing agent is an Attendee of the master object
effects: Attendee proposes a change via COUNTER
Organizer accepts by issuing a new REQUEST or refuses via DECLINECOUNTER
Ownership of the master object is not transferred

composition.purpose: A task may reference a plan or schedule entry as the intention it carries out; the plan remains independently versioned. Known relation: Task references plan or schedule because the plan is independently versioned, and task identity and work-item state stay in WM-ACT-006.

Recorded acts realize planned steps, enabling comparison of intention with performance without storing performance inside the plan. P-Plan correspondsToStep and PROV activity-versus-plan association are the primary correspondence pattern; acts remain in the act sibling.

A project may bind its schedule and baselines from this model; the project container is not itself a plan. ISO 21502 treats schedule as a project-management practice area and RFC 9253 adds project-management temporal relations to calendar items, while the project aggregate stays a sibling.

A planned instance may instantiate a standing process or protocol definition; the definition is not an intention bound to time. FHIR CarePlan.instantiatesCanonical points at PlanDefinition or similar, and CarePlan is a specific intent rather than a generic protocol.

Planning agents, organizers, attendees, approvers and beneficiaries reference person identities; calendar addresses are not person master records. PROV Person and iCalendar calendar-user addresses are associations to agents, not duplicates of a person model.
Organizations may be planning agents, organizers or CUTYPE=GROUP members. PROV Organization and iTIP group attendees are agent references.

Align calendar component, recurrence, free-busy, classification, attendee and identity properties; do not treat ICS syntax as the model. RFC 5545 is the primary calendaring object specification, and recurrence expansion ambiguities are recorded as conflicts rather than hidden.

Align Event, Task, Group, LocalDateTime, timeZone, recurrenceOverrides, relatedTo and RFC 3339 UTCDateTime. JSCalendar is the IETF JSON calendar data model and the source of this-and-future split semantics and clarified recurrence.
Align scheduling methods, organizer and attendee workflow, SEQUENCE rules and message ordering. iTIP is the application protocol for group scheduling independent of transport.
Align precedence types, GAP lead and lag, REFID grouping and LINK. RFC 9253 is the primary source for project-style temporal relations on calendar components.
Align plan-as-entity, association hadPlan, revision, generation, invalidation and attribution. PROV-DM and PROV-O define Plan but leave step structure to extensions.
Align Plan, Step, Variable, isPreceededBy and correspondsToStep or correspondsToVariable. P-Plan is the primary scientific extension that structures plans and links them to execution traces.

Align healthcare-specific intention instance, status, intent strength, partOf, basedOn, replaces and activity references. FHIR CarePlan is a primary instance-level care intention resource; PlanDefinition remains out of scope.

Align Instant, ProperInterval, duration, TRS and Allen interval relations used to interpret scheduled intervals. OWL-Time is the primary temporal topology vocabulary and the source of non-Gregorian TRS support beyond CALSCALE.

Align the practice of sequencing activities and maintaining a schedule baseline inside project management, without claiming ISO conformance. ISO 21502:2020 is paywalled, so only catalogue-level guidance is cited and baseline naming is an alignment with an evidence gap on the full text.

owner_package_requirements: The owning package publishes an AGENTS.md carrying Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL.
The owning package names the recurrence expansion profile it uses, because RFC 5545 recurrence expansion is documented as ambiguous across implementations.
The owning package records external standard alignments as ALIGN and does not claim a conformant interchange round trip without stored mapping evidence.
The owning package retains cancelled, revoked and invalidated plan versions for audit of commitments and of intention-versus-act divergence unless a documented purge policy and legal basis apply.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Plan, planned step, schedule entry, commitment, recurrence, baseline and share-grant terms are namespaced under the registry entry vr.wm-act-008. Calendaring, provenance, workflow-plan and care-intention vocabularies (iCalendar, JSCalendar, PROV, P-Plan, FHIR, OWL-Time) keep their own namespaces and are referenced as alignments rather than copied into the model namespace; status codes are always stored with the vocabulary that supplied them.
registry_links: WM-ACT-008 - model identifier for the Plan / Schedule aggregate

canonicalization_rules: Absolute times are canonicalised to RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or uppercase Z, following JSCalendar UTCDateTime.
Local civil times are stored with an IANA Time Zone Database identifier or explicitly marked as floating; a stored zone identifier is never replaced by a single numeric offset.
A recurrence UNTIL value is canonicalised to the value type of the start, and is expressed in UTC when the start is zoned.
An entry stores either an explicit end or a duration, never both, and DTEND for DATE values is exclusive.
Occurrences are canonically addressed as master identifier plus recurrence identifier, never as a bare date used as a surrogate key.
patch_rules: Per-occurrence changes are stored as recurrence overrides keyed by recurrence identifier, following the JSCalendar PatchObject diff model, rather than by cloning the master item.
A this-and-future change truncates the original series and creates a new master linked by first and next relations; it is a new master identity, not a patch of the original.
An Organizer change to DTSTART, DTEND, DURATION, DUE, RRULE, RDATE, EXDATE or STATUS increments SEQUENCE and carries a new stamp time.
Baseline snapshots are immutable after freeze; a correction creates a new baseline rather than patching the frozen one.
Attendees do not patch the master object; they REPLY, COUNTER or send a delegation REQUEST.
compatibility_rules: A higher sequence obsoletes a lower one for the same master identifier and recurrence identifier; equal sequences tie-break on the later stamp time, and out-of-order replies are discarded against the persisted last sequence and stamp per attendee.
Consumers must be told which recurrence expansion profile is authoritative, because RFC 5545 expansion is documented as ambiguous across implementations.
Status and intent codes are stored with their source vocabulary; FHIR, iCalendar and JSCalendar status vocabularies overlap but do not coincide and must not be silently merged.
Alignment to an external standard is recorded as ALIGN and does not by itself assert a conformant interchange round trip.
Precedence relation families are kept distinct: P-Plan isPreceededBy is not interchangeable with an RFC 9253 FINISHTOSTART relation carrying a GAP.

identity_priority: UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Record event time (intended start, end, due, freeze, cancel) separately from observation or ingestion time (created, updated, DTSTAMP, generatedAtTime of a provenance record) whenever those differ. A date is not an identifier; a recurrence identifier qualifies an occurrence of a master identity but is not itself the master identity.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Occurrences of a recurring master are named by the master identifier qualified by a recurrence identifier, never by a bare date; organizer revisions of the same master are numbered by an integer sequence that starts at 0 and increments whenever time, recurrence or status properties change.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Correlate revisions by master identifier plus optional recurrence qualifier plus sequence number; a higher sequence obsoletes a lower one for the same pair, and equal sequence ties break on later stamp time. DTEND and DURATION MUST NOT both be present on the same iCalendar-aligned entry. Recurrence UNTIL must match the start value type. Named baselines are explicit snapshots, not implied by sequence increment alone.

policies: The planning agent owns plans, schedule entries and commitments; beneficiaries may verify commitments made to them but cannot mutate the master object except via REPLY, COUNTER or delegated REQUEST.
Cancelled, revoked or invalidated plans are retained for audit of commitments and of intention-versus-act divergence unless a documented purge policy and legal basis apply.
Free-busy and other reduced projections MUST NOT leak summary, description, attendees or assumption content.
External standard alignments are recorded as ALIGN; no interchange round-trip is claimed as conformant without a stored expansion profile and mapping evidence.

read: Owner and explicitly granted grantees may read at the granted detail level and horizon.
Beneficiaries may read commitment terms that name them.
Auditors may read cancelled and invalidated versions under audit scope.
create: Planning agent or authorized Organizer may create plans, entries, recurrence rules and baselines.
Organizer may create REQUEST and PUBLISH scheduling messages.
Attendee may create REPLY, COUNTER, REFRESH and delegation REQUEST messages only.
update: Organizer updates the master object and MUST increment sequence when time or recurrence properties or status change.
Attendee updates only their participation status via REPLY.
Baseline snapshots are immutable after freeze; corrections create a new baseline.
delete: Physical delete is denied by default; use cancel, revoke, entered-in-error or invalidate.
Purge of cancelled records requires owner plus policy owner approval and an audit record.
Dependent FIRST, NEXT and temporal links MUST be checked before purge to avoid dangling relationships.

roles.name: planning-agent
responsibilities: Owns the plan and its schedule entries.
Adopts, revises, baselines and abandons plans.

roles.name: organizer
responsibilities: Increments sequence on significant time or status changes.

roles.name: attendee-or-beneficiary
responsibilities: Verifies existence and terms of commitments made to them.

roles.name: baseline-approver
responsibilities: Authorizes comparison snapshots used for variance.

roles.name: auditor
responsibilities: Reviews access exceptions and scheduling-message authentication.

access.default_rule: Deny all except the planning agent and Organizer on objects they own; every other read or write requires an explicit grant, a beneficiary verification right, or a recorded exception.
exceptions: Beneficiary verification of a named commitment without exposing unrelated plan content.
Break-glass clinical or safety read of a CarePlan-aligned instance, always audited.
Legal hold preventing cancel-to-purge of a commitment or baseline.
Public CLASS or JSCalendar public items readable at the published detail level.
audit_requirements: Record who read which projection at what time, including free-busy reads.
Record every SEQUENCE increment, method, cancel, revoke, baseline freeze and this-and-future split with event time and ingestion time.
Record access exceptions with acting agent, justification and expiry.

coverage.claim: This structure is a defensible wide union of primary calendaring, provenance-plan, scientific workflow-plan, care-intention and temporal-topology sources for intentions bound to time. It is not a universal ontology of planning, not a project-management body of knowledge, and not a claim of conformance to iCalendar, JSCalendar, PROV, P-Plan, FHIR or ISO 21502.

checklist.notes: Master-system id, UID or uid, governed IRI and Dimension ULID; recurrence id is a qualifier not a master key; dates are not identifiers.
Union of FHIR CarePlan status and intent, iCalendar STATUS, JSCalendar status, iTIP methods, cancel versus revoke versus invalidate.
RFC 9253 precedence and hierarchy, P-Plan isPreceededBy, FHIR partOf basedOn replaces, correspondsToStep, task and act references.
Start, end, due, duration, recurrence, time zones, OWL-Time intervals, RFC 3339 stamps, event time versus observation time.
PROV attribution, association hadPlan, revision, generation, invalidation, product identifier, DTSTAMP sequencing.
Planning agent owns; Organizer owns the master scheduling object; beneficiaries verify; SENT-BY does not transfer ownership.
DTEND exclusive of DURATION, UNTIL type matching, sequence increment rules, recurrence skip, dangling-link checks.
CLASS and privacy, free-busy versus full projections, grants, iTIP spoofing controls, break-glass exceptions.
Cancel and revoke retain records; purge is exceptional; invalidatedAtTime; legal hold.
ALIGN to RFC 5545, 5546, 8984, 9253, PROV, P-Plan, FHIR CarePlan, OWL-Time and ISO 21502 with explicit conflicts.
RRULE, RDATE, EXDATE, JSCalendar overrides, rscale and skip; expansion-profile required because RFC 5545 is ambiguous.
Participation obligation and stated terms; full commercial contracts excluded.
Named snapshot distinct from SEQUENCE; ISO 21502 cited only at catalogue level.

known_omissions: RFC 7953 VAVAILABILITY working-availability components were not fetched and are not modelled beyond free-busy.
VALARM and JSCalendar alerts are notification mechanics, not modelled as first-class findings.
RFC 7529 non-Gregorian recurrence is represented only through JSCalendar rscale and skip, not as a standalone fetched source.
PMBOK schedule-baseline and earned-value formulae were not used as primary text because the full PMI guides are paywalled and the PMI library fetch was blocked.
ISO 21502 full text is paywalled; schedule-baseline language is catalogue-level alignment only.
Critical-chain buffers, resource leveling, MRP and ISA-95 operations schedules lack primary support here.
PDDL, HTN and other automated-planning operator models are omitted.
Shift rostering, crew pairing, court and legislative calendars and military OPORD formats are omitted as specialised siblings.
CalDAV, iMIP and JSCalendar sharing protocols are interfaces, not included as semantics.
conflicts: iCalendar recurrence expansion is documented by RFC 8984 as ambiguous across implementations; JSCalendar restates the algorithm and is the preferred expansion profile when both apply.
iCalendar SEQUENCE is an organizer revision counter and is not a named ISO or PMI schedule baseline.
P-Plan isPreceededBy is transitive and untyped; RFC 9253 distinguishes four precedence types plus GAP. Treating them as identical is incorrect.
FHIR CarePlan.intent proposal is not the same as iCalendar STATUS TENTATIVE.
OWL-Time discusses leap seconds in ISO 8601; JSCalendar and iCalendar duration arithmetic MUST NOT consider leap seconds.
iCalendar DTEND for DATE values is exclusive; some project-scheduling tools treat finish dates as inclusive.
iCalendar default CLASS is PUBLIC; many enterprise calendars assume private. This model does not default to public.
PROV Plan has no recurrence, free-busy or attendee model; calendar objects have no hadPlan association. Union is alignment, not a single type.
regional_assumptions: Default calendar scale is Gregorian (iCalendar CALSCALE, JSCalendar rscale default).
Default week start is Monday in JSCalendar firstDayOfWeek default mo; US deployments often use Sunday and MUST store WKST explicitly.
Time zone interpretation assumes IANA TZDB regional rules, which change; stored zone identifiers must not be replaced by a single numeric offset.
FHIR CarePlan R4 status and intent vocabularies are used; R5 differences are not modelled.
Working weeks, holidays and prayer-time calendars are not assumed; they appear only if encoded as recurrence exceptions or free-busy.
adversarial_checks: Checked that completed acts are not stored here and that correspondsToStep is a reference to the act sibling.
Checked that standing process definitions and FHIR PlanDefinition remain out of scope.
Checked that UID plus recurrence id is not collapsed into a date used as an identifier.
Checked that SEQUENCE is not silently treated as a named baseline.
Checked that free-busy projections cannot be used to reconstruct summary or attendee lists.
Checked that resource CUTYPE rooms are participation classifications, not a duplicate resource model.
Checked that ISO 21502 and PMI claims are marked secondary or omitted rather than presented as fetched normative text.
